transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-11-25 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (EchoWorks Principal Engineer), Ava Moreno (EchoWorks Product), Samir Patel (EchoWorks Security)

Summary:
High-level handoff of marketplace listing and on-prem reference architecture for EchoWorks' LLM gateway integration. Focus areas: authentication options (OIDC/SAML/MTLS), KMS compatibility for customer-managed keys, Helm packaging and CI/CD for listing, and runbook for canary routing and fallback to Redwood hosted variants. Agreed to a follow-up lab and to exchange runbook/values.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing checklist and certs
- On-prem Helm packaging and values for air-gapped deploys
- Auth flows (SSO, token exchange, MTLS) and audit log surface area
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation
- Canary routing and rollback playbook
- Quantization and runtime tradeoffs for edge nodes

Links referenced:
- Redwood partner runbook (internal): https://redwood-internal.example/partners/runbooks/marketplace-onprem
- Draft Helm chart repo: https://git.example/redwood/partner-helm-echoworks (private)
- Benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example.com/drive/benchmarks-echoworks (note: sample numbers)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have about 52 minutes, so, uh, we'll aim to cover the listing checklist, the onprem runbook, and leave time for the k m s questions. Lucas will lead the helm bits.
[00:18] Ravi: yep, sounds good. quick context — EchoWorks is planning a v1 launch targeting private deployments for three enterprise customers in Q1. They insist on customer-managed keys and audit logs retained for at least seven years.
[00:35] Maya: got it. thanks. Samir, is the seven-year requirement regulatory or customer-specific?
[00:42] Samir: regulatory — it's part of an industry compliance package for one of our contracts. also SAML is the primary SSO we use, but OIDC is being evaluated.
[00:50] Lucas: ok, so for SAML we can support the marketplace listing flow but for the private onprem package we typically recommend OIDC + a short-lived token exchange between the onprem agent and the Redwood control plane — or if you prefer full data plane isolation we have an mtls option.
[01:08] Ava: mtls — does that require extra cert management on our side?
[01:12] Lucas: yes you'll need certs per node; we provide tooling in the helm chart to bootstrap certs from your internal CA and rotate them. brief caveat: mtls will add small latency on handshake during cold-start but then negligible for streaming.
[01:27] Ravi: understood. can you show where the KMS plug-in sits in the architecture?
[01:32] Maya: sure, I'm going to share the runbook diagram — um, in the doc the KMS adapter is between the private control plane and the HSM provider, we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, and onprem HSMs via PKCS#11.
[01:48] Samir: is the PKCS#11 approach certified? we need FIPS-ish attestations.
[01:53] Lucas: it's not a Redwood certification; it depends on your HSM vendor. we have customers using Thales and Utimaco — our connector does not hold keys, it just performs wrap/unwrap operations. we can add a sample attestation checklist for your vendor.
[02:12] Ravi: perfect. the marketplace listing will need a cert matrix — like which certs we include and which we call out as customer-managed.
[02:19] Maya: yes, we'll provide a cert matrix template. also note for the marketplace listing we require the partner to include the helm chart tarball and a verified image digest, plus a security scan report.
[02:32] Ava: about the helm tarball — do you support air-gapped installs? one of our customers is strictly air-gapped.
[02:37] Lucas: yes, chart is designed for air-gapped install: images can be preloaded, and the values file has flags to disable external lookups. we'll add an example values-echoworks-airgap.yaml.
[02:50] Maya: i'll attach the values example after the call.
[02:54] Samir: audit logging — can you stream logs to our splunk collector? we need immutable logs and tamper-evidence.
[03:01] Lucas: we support syslog forwarding and can push structured audit events to HTTP endpoints. For immutability, you'd need your log ingestion pipeline to apply WORM policies; we can tag events with immutable IDs and sequence numbers to help with verification.
[03:18] Ravi: ok good. now, on runtime: we're planning to run a small fleet of 4 A100-equivalent GPUs in an onprem cluster. we care about latency <200ms p50 for short chat prompts. any tuning notes?
[03:32] Lucas: a few things — model variant selection, kv cache warmup, and batching. for low latency we recommend smaller batch targets and a quantized fp16 or int8 variant. our runtime supports layer-wise fused attention which helps for middle-size contexts.
[03:48] Maya: also consider prefix caching if you have a lot of repeated system prompt. that can drop per-token work substantially.
[03:54] Ravi: noted.
[03:57] Ava: can Redwood provide a canary plan for model rollouts via the marketplace listing? we want to do A/B with fallback to hosted if something breaks.
[04:06] Maya: yes, our listing supports canary flags — you can route X% to the new onprem canary, Y% to the current model; if latency or error rate breaches we auto-fallback to the hosted variant. we'll share our canary playbook.
[04:20] Lucas: quick note — fallback requires a network path to Redwood hosted; if you must be fully air-gapped we can provision a local fallback to a previous onprem image instead.
[04:32] Samir: we need all of those failover modes documented.
[04:35] Maya: absolutely.
[04:37] [--- 10 minute marker summary omitted in meeting export ---]
[04:40] Lucas: going into the helm specifics — the chart has three main components: control-plane (operator), runtime pods, and edge-proxy. values allow: k m s config, mtls toggles, sso config (saml/oidc), and resource profiles for quantized runtimes.
[04:55] Ravi: does the operator require cluster-admin privileges? we try to limit RBAC scope.
[04:59] Lucas: operator needs to create CRDs and watch pods; minimum we ask for create/update on CRDs and configmaps. we provide a scripted limited-rbac manifest if you can't grant cluster-admin.
[05:13] Ava: CI/CD — we want to integrate with our existing gitlab pipelines. do you have a registry sync tool?
[05:19] Maya: yes, we can provide an example pipeline that packages the chart, signs it, uploads to your internal registry, and triggers an image pre-pull job.
[05:27] Samir: signing — do you support cosign?
[05:29] Lucas: cosign is supported, and for image verification we check digest signatures during install.
[05:34] Ravi: on metrics — what telemetry do you require to be sent back to Redwood? some customers don't want any telemetry leaving.
[05:41] Maya: default telemetry is opt-in; for marketplace certification we ask for a heartbeat and anonymized health metrics. for enterprise customers we can field a dedicated agreement: heartbeat only, or on-prem only telemetry with no external egress.
[05:56] Samir: good. legal will want an explicit list.
[06:00] Maya: we'll send the telemetry data map.
[06:03] Ava: can we run a 2-hour lab where Redwood helps configure mtls + KMS with our lab HSM?
[06:08] Lucas: yes — proposed week of Dec 6. Lucas: lab goal: deploy helm, enable KMS via PKCS#11, perform key wrap test, and run a short perf sweep.
[06:20] Ravi: sounds good.
[06:22] Maya: recapping next steps — Lucas will produce trimmed Helm values and an air-gap example; Maya will share pricing ballpark and marketplace checklist; Samir will upload the KMS vendor policy.
[06:34] Samir: i will, yes.
[06:36] Ava: one more question — are there known issues with quantized models and certain HSMs? we've heard mixed stories.
[06:43] Lucas: quantization is independent of HSMs; the only intersection is key-protected model weights if you plan to encrypt model files at rest with KMS. some older HSM connectors are slower on crypto ops which can impact key wrap speeds during startup — we will note that in the runbook.
[06:59] Ravi: how about E2E tests? can Redwood provide a smoke test harness for our CI?
[07:05] Maya: yes we have a test harness that runs a set of smoke prompts and validates latency, correctness, and token accounting. we'll provide it as a repo.
[07:14] Lucas: Also recommend a small deterministic eval set for quality regression checks during canaries.
[07:20] Maya: ok, last piece — marketplace listing metadata: we need a short description, allowed regions, supported deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and a list of required docs. we'll send a template.
[07:31] Ava: we'll fill that out and return.
[07:34] Maya: anything else?
[07:36] Ravi: maybe competitors — we looked at OtherCloudAI and EdgeServe. they had slightly different auth models and price points, so we want to highlight key diffs in the listing.
[07:48] Maya: makes sense, we'll draft a competitor positioning note.
[07:52] [Wrap and explicit next steps]
[07:55] Maya: ok thanks everyone. quick recap in chat: Lucas helm values (due Dec 3), Maya pricing and checklist (Nov 30), Samir KMS policy (Nov 30), schedule lab for week of Dec 6. I'll follow up with calendar invite and links.
[08:12] Ava: thanks all.
[08:15] Ravi: thanks.
[08:17] Samir: thanks.

End of transcript.
